papers.version_note: The text is a web page listing about 35 publication entries with short abstracts, not a single paper. The abstracts are those of other works.
papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc. resource-library page listing publications, patents and reports on quantum communications from 2006 onward.

assertions.value: The listed abstract states that the authors demonstrate the first quantum frequency conversion temporal mode sorting system in a four-dimensional Hilbert space, with a conversion efficiency and mode separability as high as 92% and 0.84.
quotes: We demonstrate the first QFC temporal mode sorting system in a four-dimensional Hilbert space, achieving a conversion efficiency and mode separability as high as 92% and 0.84, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: A listed abstract on a vendor site; the paper itself is not in this text.

assertions.value: The listed abstract states that the authors demonstrate direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs at room temperature with 3.2 um wavelength spacing, one photon at 780 nm and the other at 3950 nm.
quotes: Here, we demonstrate direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs at room temperature with 3.2 um wavelength spacing, one at 780 nm to match the rubidium D2 line, and the other at 3950 nm that falls in a transparent, low-scattering optical window for free space applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: A listed abstract on a vendor site; the paper itself is not in this text.

assertions.value: The listed abstract proposes an interaction-free all-optical quantum switch built on a chi-2 microdisk. As an example it gives a GaAs microdisk with an intrinsic Q of ~10^8 that can achieve low-loss (<~1%) switching for gigahertz-rate O-band quantum signals. This is a proposal, with no measurement stated.
quotes: We propose a quantum switch for telecom-band applications that is composed of a χ^(2) microdisk coupled to two fibers (or waveguides).
As an example, a 2.5-μm-thick, 10μm radius GaAs microdisk with an intrinsic Q of ∼10^8 and a fiber-cavity-coupling Q of ∼10^4 can achieve low-loss (≲1%) switching
